bug_semantics: search_files checked the literal user-supplied glob for a slash-delimited '..' segment before calling fast-glob, but did not validate the paths produced by glob expansion. A pattern such as '{a,..}/SECRET.txt' contains no literal '..' segment, passes the check, and can expand to '../SECRET.txt'; the tool then joined that result to the resolved working directory and either returned the outside filename or read matching lines from the outside file, disclosing files readable by the n8n OS user.
flaw_origin: PR #30670 replaced the parent implementation's bounded readdir-based collectFiles traversal with fastGlob(name, { cwd: resolvedDir }) and added only assertPatternStaysInside(name). The new pre-expansion lexical check rejected explicit absolute paths and literal '..' segments, but the result path was consumed by path.join(resolvedDir, fp) without post-expansion canonicalization or containment checking. That change first created the advisory's path-confinement bypass.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories/GHSA-pf2q-pxhf-hgmw describes arbitrary local-file disclosure through a crafted search_files pattern and identifies patched versions 2.31.5 and 2.32.1; the bundle aliases this lifecycle to CVE-2026-72773 / GHSA-cgh8-xfc3-8rm5.

git log --all --follow on packages/@n8n/computer-use/src/tools/filesystem/search-files.ts led from the July security bundles to squash landing 5476637edef52d5f3406492c764aea09725c8589 (PR #30670). GitHub's PR commits endpoint https://api.github.com/repos/n8n-io/n8n/pulls/30670/commits decomposes that squash to its sole member 99ca232e2d31f6e6ae69688a674d1e3425f8ca74, parent 06197a057d1b3155f8ca1df69bad21014c42b6a3.

The BIC patch at https://api.github.com/repos/n8n-io/n8n/commits/99ca232e2d31f6e6ae69688a674d1e3425f8ca74 adds fastGlob(name), assertPatternStaysInside(name), and path.join(resolvedDir, fp). It validates only the unexpanded pattern and performs no containment check on each glob result. PR #30670's body independently states that the change replaced the custom implementation with fast-glob and introduced the name glob parameter.

Immediate-parent tree verification against https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n8n-io/n8n/06197a057d1b3155f8ca1df69bad21014c42b6a3/packages/@n8n/computer-use/src/tools/filesystem/search-files.ts shows no fast-glob import, no name glob input, no lexical assertPatternStaysInside, and no joining of an expanded result. It resolves dirPath first and recursively enumerates entries from that resolved directory, so the vulnerable expansion-and-consumption mechanism is absent.

The direct source fix 97f5ba3f824019665adb81a9976174e5f778d71d changes search-files.ts to re-resolve every fast-glob result with resolveReadablePath(dir, path), discard failures, and use the validated absolutePath for stat/read; its tests model fastGlob returning '../SECRET.txt' from '{a,..}/SECRET.txt' and require that it be dropped. PR #34680 then lands that bundle on the public main line as 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624.

reasoning: The vulnerability did not originate with the initial filesystem search implementation: the verified parent enumerated files beneath an already-resolved directory. The sole pre-squash member of PR #30670 changed the trust boundary by passing an attacker-influenced glob to fast-glob, checking only its literal segments, and trusting the expanded relative paths for listing and file reads. Because brace expansion can synthesize '..' after that check, member commit 99ca232e2d31f6e6ae69688a674d1e3425f8ca74 is the smallest real BIC; 5476637edef52d5f3406492c764aea09725c8589 is only its squash landing. The immediate member parent lacks the entire mechanism, and the landing precedes the first affected 2.x tag found (2.22.0) and is present in the last vulnerable boundary tags. The July fix closes the causal gap by canonicalizing and confinement-checking every expanded match before it can be returned or read, with branch backports first appearing at 2.31.5 and 2.32.1. Finally, only the decomposed BIC commit object controls attribution: it has human author/committer identities and no AI trailer or bot identity. Later AI-marked fix bundles do not change that, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
